explanations.explanation: Yep, the holy garments are for Aaron. Verse 1 says they make them "as well as the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:1) Aaron gets his own wardrobe, and I got a hat and an apron.

Moses is close by, but he's not who the holy garments are for. Exodus 39:1 says they make "the holy garments for Aaron." Moses is the one the LORD gave the commands to, so he's the one getting the instructions, not the outfits.

Joshua is a good name to think of, but he's not in this verse at all. The text says the holy garments are for Aaron (Exodus 39:1). Sometimes a name just wanders into the kitchen when nobody invited it.

Not quite. The workers don't pick the look they like best. Verse 1 says they made the garments "just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:1) So these designs came with instructions, and nobody got to freestyle.

Right, it's false. The text says they made the garments "just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:1) That's the plan they follow, start to finish. No workers deciding the fringe needs a little extra something.

explanations.answer: They hammer it thin and cut threads
explanations.explanation: That's it. Verse 3 says, "They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut threads from them to interweave with the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen." (Exodus 39:3) Gold thread, y'all. The text calls it the work of a skilled craftsman, and I believe it.

explanations.answer: They melt it and pour it on
explanations.explanation: Pouring melted gold on cloth sounds like a very expensive disaster, and the text doesn't say that. Exodus 39:3 says they hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut threads from them. Then the threads were interwoven with the yarn and linen.

explanations.answer: They grind it and dye with it
explanations.explanation: Grinding gold into dye is a fun idea, but that's not what the verse says. Exodus 39:3 says they "hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut threads from them." So it's real gold thread, woven right in.

Yes, true. Verse 5 says the waistband "was of one piece with the ephod, of the same workmanship." (Exodus 39:5) No stitching on a separate belt later. It's all one piece, just like the LORD had commanded Moses.

It's actually true. Verse 5 says the skillfully woven waistband "was of one piece with the ephod, of the same workmanship." (Exodus 39:5) So it isn't a separate belt added on. It's woven right along with the rest.

explanations.answer: The names of the sons of Israel
explanations.explanation: Right. The stones were "engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel." (Exodus 39:6) Names, carved in onyx and set in gold. That's some careful handwriting.

explanations.answer: The words of the Ten Commandments
explanations.explanation: The Ten Commandments are a big deal, but they're not what's carved here. Exodus 39:6 says the onyx stones were engraved "with the names of the sons of Israel." Names, not commandments.

explanations.answer: The names of Moses and Aaron
explanations.explanation: That's a good guess, but Moses and Aaron aren't the names on these stones. Verse 6 says they were engraved "with the names of the sons of Israel." (Exodus 39:6)

Yes, memorial. Verse 7 says they fastened the stones on the shoulder pieces "as memorial stones for the sons of Israel." (Exodus 39:7) The text doesn't say more than that, so I'll leave it right there.

Foundation is a solid word, but it's not the one in the verse. Exodus 39:7 says the stones were fastened on the shoulder pieces "as memorial stones for the sons of Israel." They sit on the shoulders, not under a building.
Boundary stones are a thing, but not in this verse. Exodus 39:7 says these were "memorial stones for the sons of Israel." Same stones, different word.

True. Verse 8 says, "He made the breastpiece with the same workmanship as the ephod, with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen." (Exodus 39:8) It's the same fancy materials and the same skill, matching from top to bottom.
It's true, actually. Exodus 39:8 says the breastpiece was made "with the same workmanship as the ephod." Gold, blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and fine linen, all of it matching.

explanations.answer: The name of one of the tribes
explanations.explanation: Yes. Verse 14 says each stone "was engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 39:14) Twelve stones, twelve names, one each. Nobody gets two and nobody gets left out.
A promise would be lovely, but that's not what's on the stones. Exodus 39:14 says each stone was engraved with "the name of one of the twelve tribes." One tribe name per stone.
No law lines here. Verse 14 says each of the twelve stones was "engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes." (Exodus 39:14) Just a name, small and sharp.

explanations.answer: So it won't swing out from the ephod
explanations.explanation: That's the reason the text gives. Verse 21 says they tied the rings together with blue cord "so that the breastpiece was above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing out from the ephod." (Exodus 39:21) It stays put, right where it belongs.

explanations.answer: So it can come off in a hurry
explanations.explanation: The text goes the other direction. Exodus 39:21 says the cord was there so the breastpiece "would not swing out from the ephod." Nothing in the verse says it was meant to come off quickly.

explanations.answer: So the stones won't scratch the linen
explanations.explanation: Scratching is a fair worry, but the text doesn't say it. Verse 21 gives the reason: so the breastpiece "was above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing out from the ephod." (Exodus 39:21)
Yes, blue. Verse 22 says, "They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth, the work of a weaver." (Exodus 39:22) One color, all the way through.
Scarlet shows up elsewhere in the garments, but not for this robe. Exodus 39:22 says the robe was made "entirely of blue cloth." Scarlet only joins in later, on the pomegranates.
Purple's in the yarn on other pieces, but this robe is a different story. Verse 22 says it was made "entirely of blue cloth." (Exodus 39:22) Purple does turn up on the hem, in the pomegranates.

That's right. Verse 23 says there was "a collar around the opening so that it would not tear." (Exodus 39:23) A little reinforcement, and it's a smart one. I've torn a few things by pulling too hard, so I get it.

explanations.answer: So it sits higher on the neck
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say anything about height. Exodus 39:23 says the collar was around the opening "so that it would not tear." That's the whole reason it gives.

explanations.answer: So it can be tied shut
explanations.explanation: Nothing in the verse mentions tying. Exodus 39:23 says the collar was there "so that it would not tear." It's for strength, plain and simple.

Yes, bells. Verse 25 says, "They also made bells of pure gold and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates." (Exodus 39:25) Pure gold, and they alternate with the pomegranates all the way around (Exodus 39:26).
Cymbals would be a LOT, friend. But the verse says something smaller: "bells of pure gold." (Exodus 39:25) They're attached around the hem between the pomegranates.
Horns on a hem? That'd be a parade. Exodus 39:25 says they made "bells of pure gold" and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates.
Not quite. Verse 27 says, "For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver." (Exodus 39:27) So Aaron's sons get tunics too. The whole family gets dressed.
Right, false. The text says "For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver." (Exodus 39:27) Aaron's sons are included, so nobody's standing around in the cold.
Yes. Verse 30 says they engraved on the plate, "like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD." (Exodus 39:30) Pure gold, with those words on it. Big message, small plate.
Servant is a good word, but it's not what's engraved. Exodus 39:30 says the inscription reads "HOLY TO THE LORD." That's what goes on the gold plate.
That sounds like it would fit, but it's not in the text. Verse 30 says the gold plate was engraved, "HOLY TO THE LORD." (Exodus 39:30)
Yep, the turban. Verse 31 says, "Then they fastened to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:31) Blue cord, gold plate, turban. All set.
The sash is another linen piece, but it's not where the plate goes. Exodus 39:31 says the blue cord was fastened "to mount it on the turban." The sash is in verse 29, and it has its own job.
The breastpiece has its own gold and cords, but this plate isn't on it. Verse 31 says the blue cord was fastened to the plate "to mount it on the turban." (Exodus 39:31)

True. Verse 32 says, "So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Exodus 39:32) Last piece done, and the work is complete.
It's actually true. Right after the holy crown, verse 32 says, "So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed." (Exodus 39:32) Nothing left on the list.

That's it. Verse 43 says Moses "inspected all the work and saw that they had accomplished it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them." (Exodus 39:43) After all that inspecting, a blessing is a pretty great way to end.

explanations.answer: He gives them a day off
explanations.explanation: A day off sounds nice, but the text doesn't say it. Exodus 39:43 says Moses saw they'd done it just as the LORD commanded, "So Moses blessed them." That's what he does.
A feast would be fun, and I'd bring cookies, but the verse doesn't say it. Exodus 39:43 says, "So Moses blessed them." A blessing is what comes next.
